newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: S.Korea threatens to deport world labour leaders.
newsitem.headline: S.Korea threatens to deport world labour leaders.

text.p: An international labour leader said on Wednesday that the South Korean government would deport him and three colleagues if they had any more contact with trade union leaders directing nationwide strikes in South Korea.

International Metalworkers' Federation (IMWF) Secretary-General Marcello Malentacchi said an immigration official had told them: "Any participation or contact with Korean union leaders would be considered in violation of the law and result in deportation."
Malentacchi told Reuters the immigration official had given him a letter from the Ministry of Justice which outlined the laws they would be violating.

Malentacchi said he and the three other international labour leaders had already been due to leave Seoul at midday on Thursday prior to receiving the government's threat. But he added they would go ahead and meet leaders of the outlawed Korean Confederation of Trade Unions several hours before their departure.

The labour leaders have been in Seoul in a show of international worker solidarity for trade unions protesting against a controversial new labour law rammed through parliament by the ruling New Korea Party on December 26.

Workers wielding iron bars and hurling rocks battled riot police on Wednesday but planned nationwide work stoppages fizzled as many others ignored strike calls. Some even pushed through picket lines to report to work.
